grammar.name: Congiuntivo presente: regular forms
grammar.scope: regular forms; after verbs of opinion (penso che, credo che, mi sembra che); contrast with secondo me + indicative

chapters.theme: Opinions, discussions at the bar, current affairs
chapters.a_plot: Nadia has taken the job as manager of a pharmacy in Milan; Matteo is at home with baby Anna and the bar. Everyone at the bar has an opinion about it, and says it.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, now in quarta, has to choose a topic for a debate class. She picks 'Is it better to stay or to leave?'
chapters.arc: Season premiere: new family balance; the theme of choosing is set.

grammar.name: Congiuntivo presente: irregular forms
grammar.scope: sia, abbia, vada, faccia, possa, voglia, debba, sappia, dica, venga, stia, dia; pare che / si dice che

chapters.a_plot: A rumour runs down Via dei Tigli: Roberto will run for the town council. 'Pare che abbia già una lista!' It's true.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia returns from the honeymoon in Puglia to find that everyone thinks she's pregnant, at sixty-one. Ornella started the rumour by accident.

title.en: They Want Me to Come Back

grammar.name: Subjunctive after will and desire
grammar.scope: volere che, preferire che, sperare che, desiderare che, chiedere che; same subject → infinitive vs different subject → che + subjunctive

chapters.a_plot: An email from Chicago: Ben's old company wants him back as marketing director. Double the salary, a house, a car. They want him to start in March.
chapters.b_plot: Ben doesn't tell anyone. He tells Ornella, who tells him she hopes he tells Chiara tonight.

grammar.name: Subjunctive after emotions
grammar.scope: essere contento/felice/triste che, avere paura che, dispiacere che, temere che, stupirsi che; same-subject infinitive (ho paura di partire)

chapters.theme: Feelings, family reactions, fear of change
chapters.a_plot: Ben tells the family. Chiara is proud and terrified; Emma is furious that she's being asked to leave again; Leo is excited about Chicago. Franco says nothing, and leaves.
chapters.b_plot: Franco goes to the cemetery and talks to Anna about 'l'americano'. He's afraid he'll lose his grandchildren, and his son.

grammar.name: Subjunctive after impersonal expressions
grammar.scope: è importante che, è necessario che, bisogna che, è meglio che, è possibile che, è normale che; with infinitive when general

chapters.a_plot: Chiara and Ben make a list of pros and cons on the kitchen wall. The whole family adds items, including Franco, secretly, at night.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto asks Ben to be his campaign manager: 'È importante che la campagna sia moderna.' Ben is the only marketing expert on the street.

grammar.name: Subjunctive after conjunctions
grammar.scope: benché, sebbene, perché (purpose), affinché, prima che, senza che, a meno che, purché; prima di / senza + infinitive with the same subject

chapters.a_plot: The campaign starts: flyers, a slogan, a social media plan. Roberto hates everything 'modern', 'benché' it works.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo decides to run too, against Roberto, just to annoy him. Then he gets 200 followers in a day.
chapters.runner: Roberto's slogan drafts, each longer than the one before.

title.it: So che è vero, ma credo che...
title.en: I Know It's True, But I Think...

grammar.name: Subjunctive or indicative?
grammar.scope: certainty (so che, è vero che, sono sicuro che + indicative) vs doubt/opinion (non so se, dubito che, non è vero che + subjunctive); spoken usage

chapters.a_plot: Emma researches universities in Italy and the US. She is sure of one thing only: she doesn't want her parents to decide for her.
chapters.b_plot: Leo, now 10, asks everyone if they are sure about God, about Chicago, and about whether Pavarotti the cat is immortal.
chapters.arc: Emma's version of the Chicago question.

grammar.name: Congiuntivo passato
grammar.scope: formation (abbia fatto, sia andato); past actions after verbs requiring the subjunctive; time relations present/past

chapters.theme: Accidents, the elderly, the health system
chapters.a_plot: Ornella doesn't open her shutters one morning. Ben breaks in: she has fallen and broken her hip. At the hospital, everyone wonders how long she's been on the floor.
chapters.b_plot: Ornella's only relative, a niece in Genoa, thinks it's time Ornella moved into a care home. The street disagrees.

title.en: If I Win, I'll Change Everything

grammar.name: Hypothetical sentences, type 1 (real)
grammar.scope: se + present → present/future/imperative; se + future → future; real possibilities

chapters.a_plot: The candidates' debate at the Centro civico. Roberto promises order; Matteo promises free coffee; the mayor promises everything.
chapters.b_plot: The street organises shifts to help Ornella at home: if she has help, she can stay. Everyone signs up.
chapters.arc: Election campaign peak. The street as family.

grammar.name: Congiuntivo imperfetto: forms
grammar.scope: regular forms; irregular fossi, dessi, stessi, facessi, dicessi, bevessi; after past-tense main verbs (volevo che, pensavo che); se fossi in te

chapters.a_plot: Ben's old friend Mike from Chicago visits and paints a picture of the life Ben could have. Ben catches himself defending Borgoverde.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara admits to Nadia that she wanted Ben to say no immediately, and she never thought she would feel that.

grammar.name: Hypothetical sentences, type 2 (possible/imaginary)
grammar.scope: se + congiuntivo imperfetto → condizionale presente; imagining alternatives; contrast with type 1

chapters.a_plot: At Sunday lunch, everyone imagines the Carters' life in Chicago in detail. The fantasy gets funnier, then sadder.
chapters.b_plot: Leo imagines what he would do if he were mayor of Borgoverde; the kids at school vote for him in a mock election.
chapters.runner: Franco: 'Se fossi il sindaco, vieterei il ketchup.'

grammar.name: Magari, come se + subjunctive
grammar.scope: magari + congiuntivo imperfetto (wishes); come se + congiuntivo imperfetto/trapassato; magari as 'maybe' + indicative

chapters.a_plot: Everyone behaves 'come se' nothing is happening. The Christmas preparations are too cheerful, and Emma calls it out.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo, the candidate, starts taking it seriously: 'Magari vincessi!' Nadia is alarmed.
chapters.runner: Ornella, home with a walker, acts as if she has never been ill.

grammar.name: Indefinite expressions + subjunctive
grammar.scope: chiunque, qualunque/qualsiasi, dovunque, comunque (however) + subjunctive; qualunque cosa succeda

chapters.a_plot: Christmas. Everyone privately assumes the Carters will leave and gives them 'memory' gifts. Franco's gift is a photo album: 'Dovunque andiate.'
chapters.b_plot: Ornella hosts Christmas lunch for the first time in years, 'chiunque venga', and the whole street comes.
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: the Christmas of goodbyes that might not happen.

grammar.name: Subjunctive in relative clauses
grammar.scope: cerco qualcuno che sappia, non c'è nessuno che possa, l'unico che + subjunctive; contrast with indicative for real people

chapters.a_plot: Matteo needs a barista who can do everything Ben does, 'nel caso' Ben leaves. He writes an ad; the candidates are a disaster.
chapters.b_plot: Ornella needs a carer. She interviews them like a prosecutor and hires Irina, a Ukrainian nurse, who has a sense of humour.

title.it: Il più bel ricordo che abbia

grammar.name: Superlatives + subjunctive
grammar.scope: il più ... che + subjunctive (il più bel posto che abbia mai visto); il primo/l'ultimo/l'unico che

chapters.theme: Memories, reviews, the best and the worst
chapters.a_plot: Leo's school project: 'The best day of my life'. He interviews the whole family, and all their best days happened in Borgoverde.
chapters.b_plot: Ben writes a review of Bar Tigli as a joke ('Il peggior caffè che abbia mai bevuto: 5 stelle') and it goes viral locally.
chapters.arc: The answer starts to reveal itself.

grammar.name: Comparisons with the subjunctive
grammar.scope: più/meno ... di quanto + subjunctive (è più difficile di quanto pensassi); meglio di quanto credessi; expectations vs reality

chapters.a_plot: Matteo and Nadia: one year of parenthood is harder than they thought. Nadia's new job, Matteo's campaign, baby Anna's teeth. They have their first real fight.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara visits the Chicago office on a video call, and it's smaller than she expected.

grammar.name: Expressing agreement and disagreement
grammar.scope: sono d'accordo / non sono d'accordo, hai ragione ma..., non è detto che + subjunctive, dal mio punto di vista, al contrario, invece; turn-taking in debate

chapters.a_plot: The final debate before the election, broadcast on local TV. Ben coaches Roberto; Matteo improvises; the mayor is untouchable.
chapters.b_plot: Emma wins her school debate by arguing for staying. Ben watches the video and cries.

grammar.name: Formal letters: complaints and requests
grammar.scope: structure of formal complaints; expressions (con la presente, sono a segnalare, La prego di, distinti saluti); formal register and subjunctive

chapters.a_plot: Ornella, in a wheelchair for now, can't get down the pavement of Via dei Tigli. Ben, Roberto and Ornella write a formal complaint to the mayor, which becomes a campaign issue.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia writes a formal complaint to the tram company about Franco's pension. Franco thinks it's hopeless. It isn't.
chapters.arc: Ornella's accessibility becomes the election's local issue.

grammar.name: Understanding news language
grammar.scope: headline style (nominal sentences, missing articles); common news verbs (dichiarare, annunciare, rivelare); the passive as a preview

chapters.a_plot: The local paper, *La Voce di Borgoverde*, interviews Roberto and Matteo. Both articles misquote everyone.
chapters.b_plot: Emma writes for the school newspaper about the Ornella pavement story, and it's picked up by the local paper.
chapters.runner: Franco reads the paper aloud at the bar every morning, correcting its grammar.

grammar.name: Numbers, statistics and results
grammar.scope: percentages, decimals (virgola), majorities, rankings (il primo classificato); verbs for trends (aumentare, diminuire, superare, raggiungere)

chapters.theme: Election night, results, winning and losing
chapters.a_plot: Election night at Bar Tigli, with results on TV and every vote counted. Roberto is elected councillor with 11 votes to spare. Matteo gets 94 votes, 'more than I expected'.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto thanks Ben in public, using 'tu' for the first time.

grammar.name: Review: all pronoun systems
grammar.scope: direct, indirect, combined, ci, ne, reflexive, stressed; pronouns with modals, infinitives, imperatives and compound tenses

chapters.a_plot: Ornella comes home for good. The street has built a ramp (Roberto's first act as councillor). She thanks everyone, each in a different way.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara must answer Chicago this week. She and Ben go for a long walk to the old plane tree in the park.

grammar.name: The past tense system: review
grammar.scope: passato prossimo, imperfetto and trapassato prossimo together; congiuntivo passato in narration; choosing the right past tense

chapters.a_plot: Each family member tells the story of the moment they felt at home in Borgoverde, and it had already happened long before they noticed.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia and Matteo make up: she didn't know he had already sold his campaign posters to pay for her birthday gift.

grammar.name: Verbs that change meaning with prepositions
grammar.scope: pensare a / pensare di; credere a / credere in / credere di; tenere a; parlare di / parlare con; servire a / servire da; convenire

chapters.a_plot: Emma asks Ben what he believes in. His answer, in fluent Italian, surprises both of them.
chapters.b_plot: Franco, who always said he believed only in Milan and tomatoes, confesses to Lucia what he really believes in.
chapters.arc: Ben's decision, felt before it's spoken.

title.it: Che tu resti o che tu parta

grammar.name: Review: the subjunctive
grammar.scope: all uses of congiuntivo presente/passato/imperfetto; che ... o che; subjunctive vs indicative vs infinitive

chapters.a_plot: Franco finally speaks to Ben alone, in the orto: whether he stays or goes, he's family. It's what Ben needed to hear to decide.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Leo write their parents a letter with their own vote.

grammar.name: B1 review
grammar.scope: Consolidation of B1: all subjunctive uses, hypotheticals I–II, future and conditional, past system, formal writing, opinion and debate

chapters.a_plot: Ben calls Chicago with the whole family listening at the kitchen door. He declines: 'Casa mia è qui.' Then he goes to the bar, where the whole street is waiting.
chapters.b_plot: Carnevale party at the Centro civico: Roberto's first speech as councillor, and Ornella dances (sitting down).
chapters.arc: SEASON FINALE: the Carters stay. End of B1.
